content: If you are a resident of the United States, you can contact the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current medical condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your healthcare provider. Missed Dose Instructions: If you forget to take a dose, administer it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Storage Guidelines: Store this medication at room temperature, away from direct light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. For the liquid form of this medication, discard any unused portion after 7 days. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary of the medication and does not include all possible information. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete details about this medication and your individual health needs. Liquid Form Instructions: If you are taking the liquid form of this medication, shake the bottle well before each dose. Use a special measuring device or spoon to ensure accurate dosing. Children aged 11 years or younger should only take the liquid form of nitazoxanide and not the tablet form. Antibiotic Use: Antibiotics are most effective when the concentration of the medication in your body is maintained at a consistent level. Continue taking this medication for the full duration prescribed, even if your symptoms improve after a few doses. Potential Side Effects: Common side effects may include headache, nausea, or stomach/abdominal pain. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Precautions: Before taking nitazoxanide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. The liquid form of this medication contains sugar, so caution is advised if you have diabetes. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your healthcare provider. Always follow the prescribed instructions and consult your doctor for any concerns or questions.
